goal: A script that sorts the files in ~/sutra-demo/sort-me into subfolders named for each file's extension (a.pdf into pdf/, b.jpg into jpg/, c.txt into txt/, d.csv into csv/), with an automated test, and is run on that folder.

checklist.question: Does a check verify that after sort_files.py runs on a given folder, a.pdf is in the pdf/ subfolder, b.jpg is in jpg/, c.txt is in txt/ and d.csv is in csv/?
Does a check verify that each subfolder is named exactly for the file's extension (pdf, jpg, txt, csv, without a dot) and that the sorted files are moved out of the top level of the given folder?
Does a check verify that the script takes the folder to sort as a given argument, so it works on any folder rather than only one hard-coded path?
Does a check verify that test_sort_files.py runs automatically and passes, with no manual steps?
Does a check verify that test_sort_files.py asserts a.pdf ends up in pdf/, b.jpg in jpg/, c.txt in txt/ and d.csv in csv/, rather than only that the test file exists?
Does a check verify that test_sort_files.py fails when a file is not in its extension folder, for example when the script is broken or does nothing?
Does a check verify that, after the script was run on ~/sutra-demo/sort-me, a.pdf is in pdf/, b.jpg is in jpg/, c.txt is in txt/ and d.csv is in csv/ there?
Does a check verify that no sorted file is left loose in the top level of ~/sutra-demo/sort-me and that none were lost or deleted?

known_pattern.evidence: Sorting files into folders named for their extension is a standard pattern: 'sorts the files in a given folder into subfolders named for each file's extension'.

factors.name: extension-named subfolders mapping
factors.quote: sorts the files in a given folder into subfolders named for each file's extension (a.pdf into pdf/, b.jpg into jpg/, c.txt into txt/, d.csv into csv/)
factors.why: This is the core behaviour: each file goes into a subfolder named for its extension, and the script must work on any folder it is given.

factors.name: test checks the four named placements
factors.quote: checks the script puts a.pdf in pdf/, b.jpg in jpg/, c.txt in txt/ and d.csv in csv/
factors.why: The automated test must assert exactly these four placements, or it does not verify the charter.

factors.name: nothing written outside the folder
factors.why: Necessary condition C3. The script moves files only inside the folder it is given, and the test builds its fixture inside the output folder, not in a system temp location.

factors.name: no unresolved placeholders
factors.why: Necessary condition C5. Neither file may contain 'to be confirmed', TODO or similar markers.

factors.name: standard library only
factors.why: Necessary condition C2. Code reruns the test independently in a sandbox on a copy of the folder, so neither file may need packages that are not installed.

workflows.name: build_sort_script
workflows.approach: Write a standard-library Python script that moves each file in the given folder into a subfolder named for its extension.
workflows.goal: Produce sort_files.py, which takes a folder path and moves each file into a subfolder named for its extension (a.pdf into pdf/, b.jpg into jpg/, c.txt into txt/, d.csv into csv/), touching nothing outside that folder.
workflows.done_test: sort_files.py exists in the output folder; it uses only the Python standard library; it has no placeholder text such as 'to be confirmed' or TODO; it takes the folder path as an argument and runs on any given folder; and running it on a folder with a.pdf, b.jpg, c.txt and d.csv leaves a.pdf in pdf/, b.jpg in jpg/, c.txt in txt/ and d.csv in csv/ inside that folder, with nothing written outside it.

workflows.name: write_sort_test
workflows.approach: Write a standard-library unittest that builds a fixture folder inside the output folder, runs sort_files.py on it and asserts the four placements.
workflows.goal: Produce test_sort_files.py, an automated test that checks sort_files.py puts a.pdf in pdf/, b.jpg in jpg/, c.txt in txt/ and d.csv in csv/.
workflows.done_test: test_sort_files.py exists in the output folder; it uses only the standard library; it has no placeholder text; it creates its fixture folder with a.pdf, b.jpg, c.txt and d.csv inside the output folder (not in a system temp location) and removes it afterwards; it runs sort_files.py from build_sort_script on that fixture; it asserts a.pdf is in pdf/, b.jpg in jpg/, c.txt in txt/ and d.csv in csv/; and it passes when run, including on a copy of the folder.
